definition.stemRaw:
You need to deploy a new version of the LabelMaker application to ACR.  
  
Which three actions should you perform, in sequence?

slots.answer: Build a new application image by using dockerfile.
Create an alias of the image with the fully qualified path to the registry.
Log in to the registry and push image.

items: Log in to the registry and push image.
Create an alias of the image with a new build number.
Create an alias of the image with the fully qualified path to the registry.
Download the image to your local computer.
Build a new application image by using dockerfile.
definition.explanation:
A Dockerfile builds the application image. Before an image can be pushed to Azure Container Registry, it must be tagged with the registry login server and repository path; after authentication, Docker can push that tagged image. A separate build-number alias is optional and is not necessary for this sequence.

**Learn more:** [Push and pull images in Azure Container Registry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-get-started-docker-cli)

finalExplanation: A Dockerfile builds the application image. Before an image can be pushed to Azure Container Registry, it must be tagged with the registry login server and repository path; after authentication, Docker can push that tagged image. A separate build-number alias is optional and is not necessary for this sequence.

Solution: Turn on ingress, create a custom scale rule, and apply that rule to the container app.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Container Apps requires either ingress, a minimum replica count, or a custom scale rule to avoid an app with disabled ingress becoming unable to start after scaling to zero. Enabling ingress permits users to reach the app, while the custom scale rule supplies a scaling trigger that can activate replicas. [Scaling in Azure Container Apps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

**Learn more:** [Scaling in Azure Container Apps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

finalExplanation: Azure Container Apps requires either ingress, a minimum replica count, or a custom scale rule to avoid an app with disabled ingress becoming unable to start after scaling to zero. Enabling ingress permits users to reach the app, while the custom scale rule supplies a scaling trigger that can activate replicas. [Scaling in Azure Container Apps | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: Turn on ingress and set the container app's minimum replica count to 1.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Container Apps requires ingress to expose an app to incoming traffic. A minimum replica setting of 1 keeps at least one revision replica running instead of allowing the app to scale to zero, restoring availability for users.

**Learn more:** [Ingress in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/ingress-overview) · [Set scaling rules in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

finalExplanation: Azure Container Apps requires ingress to expose an app to incoming traffic. A minimum replica setting of 1 keeps at least one revision replica running instead of allowing the app to scale to zero, restoring availability for users.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: Turn on ingress, create an HTTP scale rule, and apply that rule to the container app.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Container Apps with ingress disabled can scale to zero and have no HTTP-based way to start again. Enabling ingress makes the app reachable for HTTP traffic, while an HTTP scale rule uses incoming request concurrency to scale the app out from zero. [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

**Learn more:** [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

finalExplanation: Azure Container Apps with ingress disabled can scale to zero and have no HTTP-based way to start again. Enabling ingress makes the app reachable for HTTP traffic, while an HTTP scale rule uses incoming request concurrency to scale the app out from zero. [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: Enable ingress, create a TCP scale rule, and apply that rule to the container app.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
Enabling ingress makes the container app reachable, and a TCP scaling rule can trigger replicas from incoming TCP connections even when the revision has scaled to zero. Azure Container Apps documents TCP scaling with `minReplicas` set to `0` and ingress configured for TCP traffic.

**Learn more:** [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app) · [Configure Ingress for your app in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/ingress-how-to)

finalExplanation: Enabling ingress makes the container app reachable, and a TCP scaling rule can trigger replicas from incoming TCP connections even when the revision has scaled to zero. Azure Container Apps documents TCP scaling with `minReplicas` set to `0` and ingress configured for TCP traffic.

You need to fix the VM issues. Which tools should you use?
definition.explanation:
Azure Backup creates recovery points for Azure VMs and restores VMs, disks, or files from those backups. Azure Network Watcher is used to monitor and diagnose networking rather than provide the performance enhancement itself.

Accelerated Networking improves VM network performance through single-root I/O virtualization, reducing latency, jitter, and CPU utilization. Azure Network Watcher is used to monitor and diagnose networking rather than provide the performance enhancement itself.

definition.stemRaw:
You are building a web application that uses Azure Cache for Redis. You expect the cache to fill frequently and will need to evict keys.  
  
You must configure Azure Cache for Redis for the following predicted usage pattern: a small subset of elements will be accessed much more often than the remaining elements.  
  
You need to configure Azure Cache for Redis to optimize performance for the predicted usage pattern.  
  
Which two eviction policies will meet the goal?  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
definition.explanation:
LRU eviction preserves frequently accessed keys by removing the keys that have gone unused for the longest time. `allkeys-lru` evaluates all keys, whereas `volatile-lru` evaluates keys that have an expiration set. Both therefore favor the frequently accessed subset under memory pressure.

**Learn more:** [Configure Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-configure) · [Best practices for memory management - Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-best-practices-memory-management)

finalExplanation: LRU eviction preserves frequently accessed keys by removing the keys that have gone unused for the longest time. `allkeys-lru` evaluates all keys, whereas `volatile-lru` evaluates keys that have an expiration set. Both therefore favor the frequently accessed subset under memory pressure.

definition.stemRaw:
You are building an inventory-tracking solution. The solution contains an Azure Function app with multiple functions that are triggered by Azure Cosmos DB. You plan to deploy the solution across multiple Azure regions.  
  
The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Item results from Azure Cosmos DS must return the latest committed version of an item.  
- Items written to Azure Cosmos DB must guarantee ordering.  
  
You need to configure the consistency level for the Azure Cosmos DB deployments.  
  
Which consistency level should you use?
definition.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB strong consistency provides linearizability: reads always return the most recently committed item version, and committed writes are globally ordered. The weaker consistency levels can return stale data or provide ordering guarantees only within more limited bounds or sessions.

**Learn more:** [Consistency levels in Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/consistency-levels)

finalExplanation: Azure Cosmos DB strong consistency provides linearizability: reads always return the most recently committed item version, and committed writes are globally ordered. The weaker consistency levels can return stale data or provide ordering guarantees only within more limited bounds or sessions.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing an Azure App Service-hosted ASP.NET Core web app that delivers video-on-demand streaming media. You enable Azure Content Delivery Network (CDN) Standard for the web endpoint. Customers download videos from the web app by using a URL such as `http://www.contoso.com/content.mp4?quality=1`.  
  
All media content must expire from the cache after one hour. Videos with different quality levels must be delivered from the closest regional point-of-presence (POP) node.  
  
You need to configure Azure CDN caching rules. Which options should you use?
definition.explanation:
Override enforces the configured CDN cache lifetime instead of honoring an origin-provided expiration value, ensuring that media expires after one hour. Caching every unique URL makes the `quality` query-string value part of the cache key, so each video-quality variant is cached and delivered correctly from CDN edge POPs.

**Learn more:** [az cdn endpoint rule — Azure CLI reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/cdn/endpoint/rule?view=azure-cli-latest)

finalExplanation: Override enforces the configured CDN cache lifetime instead of honoring an origin-provided expiration value, ensuring that media expires after one hour. Caching every unique URL makes the `quality` query-string value part of the cache key, so each video-quality variant is cached and delivered correctly from CDN edge POPs.

You are developing a back-end Azure App Service that scales based on the number of messages in a Service Bus queue.  
  
An existing rule scales up the App Service when the average queue length of unprocessed and valid messages exceeds 1000.  
  
Add a rule that continuously scales down the App Service whenever the scale-up condition is not met. How should you configure the Scale rule?
definition.explanation:
Active messages are the valid, unprocessed messages in the Service Bus queue. Use the Average aggregation and a scale-in condition of less than or equal to 1,000, which is the complement of the existing scale-out condition of average greater than 1,000.

**Learn more:** [Autoscale common metrics - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/autoscale/autoscale-common-metrics) · [Monitoring data reference for Azure Service Bus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/monitor-service-bus-reference)

finalExplanation: Active messages are the valid, unprocessed messages in the Service Bus queue. Use the Average aggregation and a scale-in condition of less than or equal to 1,000, which is the complement of the existing scale-out condition of average greater than 1,000.

You are developing an ASP.NET Core website that uses Azure FrontDoor. The website builds custom weather data sets for researchers. Users download the data sets as Comma Separated Value (CSV) files, and the data is refreshed every 10 hours.  
  
Specific files must be purged from the FrontDoor cache according to Response Header values.  
  
You need to purge individual assets from the Front Door cache. Which type of cache purge should you use?
definition.explanation:
Azure Front Door uses a single-path purge to remove an individual cached asset by specifying the asset’s full path, including its file extension. Wildcard purges target groups of files and folders, and a root-domain purge clears all assets for the endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Purge cache in Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/cache-purge)

finalExplanation: Azure Front Door uses a single-path purge to remove an individual cached asset by specifying the asset’s full path, including its file extension. Wildcard purges target groups of files and folders, and a root-domain purge clears all assets for the endpoint.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing an Azure-hosted application that must use a key from an on-premises hardware security module (HSM). The key must be transferred to your existing Azure Key Vault through the Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) process.  
  
You need to securely transfer the key to Azure Key Vault.  
  
Which four actions should you perform in order?

slots.answer: Retrieve the Key Exchange Key (KEK) public key.
Generate a key transfer blob file by using the HSM vendor-provided tool.
Run the az keyvault key import command.

items: Generate a key transfer blob file by using the HSM vendor-provided tool.
Create a custom policy definition in Azure Policy.
Run the az keyvault key import command.
Run the az keyvault key restore command.
Retrieve the Key Exchange Key (KEK) public key.
definition.explanation:
A KEK generated in the destination Key Vault protects the target key during transfer. Exporting the KEK public key lets the HSM vendor BYOK tool encrypt and package the on-premises key as a transfer blob; `az keyvault key import` uploads that blob, where Key Vault decrypts and imports it within its HSM boundary.

**Learn more:** [How to generate and transfer HSM-protected keys for Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/keys/hsm-protected-keys-byok)

finalExplanation: A KEK generated in the destination Key Vault protects the target key during transfer. Exporting the KEK public key lets the HSM vendor BYOK tool encrypt and package the on-premises key as a transfer blob; `az keyvault key import` uploads that blob, where Key Vault decrypts and imports it within its HSM boundary.

definition.stemRaw:
You develop and deploy several APIs in Azure API Management.  
  
You create the following policy fragment named APICounts:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783832053632-723nhkt4.png)  
  
The policy fragment must be reusable across multiple scopes and APIs. It must apply to every API and execute whenever a calling system invokes an API.  
  
You need to implement the policy fragment.
definition.template:
<policies>
  <{{section_open}}>
    <{{policy_name}} {{attribute_name}}="APICounts" />
    <base />
  </{{section_close}}>
  . . .
</policies>
definition.explanation:
A global API Management policy is inherited by all APIs. The inbound section processes incoming API calls, and the include-fragment policy inserts a reusable fragment using its required fragment-id attribute. Therefore APICounts is included as <include-fragment fragment-id="APICounts" /> in the global inbound section.

**Learn more:** [Azure API Management policy reference - include-fragment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/include-fragment-policy) · [Set or Edit Azure API Management Policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/set-edit-policies)

finalExplanation: A global API Management policy is inherited by all APIs. The inbound section processes incoming API calls, and the include-fragment policy inserts a reusable fragment using its required fragment-id attribute. Therefore APICounts is included as <include-fragment fragment-id="APICounts" /> in the global inbound section.

definition.stemRaw:
You need to configure the Account Kind, Replication, and Access tier options for the corporate website's Azure Storage account.  
  
How should you complete the configuration? Select the appropriate options in the dialog box.

finalExplanation: StorageV2 (general purpose v2) is Microsoft's recommended storage account kind for most scenarios and is required to use the Hot/Cool access tiers that help minimize storage costs, unlike the legacy general-purpose v1 kind. Geo-zone-redundant storage (GZRS) synchronously replicates data across three availability zones within the primary region (via ZRS) and asynchronously copies it to a secondary region, which is exactly what is needed when data must be both zone-redundant and geo-redundant; read-access variants (RA-GRS/RA-GZRS) add cost for secondary-region read access that isn't required here, and LRS/ZRS/GRS alone don't satisfy both the zone- and region-redundancy requirements. The Cool access tier is optimized for infrequently modified data and offers lower storage costs than the Hot tier (at the cost of slightly higher access charges), which aligns with the requirement to minimize data storage costs for the corporate website's content.

Solution: Configure Application Insights Smart Detection.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?

Application Insights Smart Detection identifies potential performance and failure anomalies, but it does not by itself configure an existing alert to execute an Azure Function. An Azure Monitor action group with an Azure Function action must be associated with the alert rule to invoke Function1 when the alert fires.

**Learn more:** [Azure Monitor action groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups) · [Smart detection in Application Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/proactive-diagnostics)

definition.stemRaw:
You develop a REST API and implement a user delegation SAS token to communicate with Azure Blob storage.  
  
The token has been compromised. You need to revoke it.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove the role assignment for the security principle.

definition.explanation:
A user delegation SAS can be revoked by revoking its user delegation key, which invalidates SAS tokens signed with that key. It can also be revoked by changing or removing the RBAC role assignment for the security principal used to create the SAS, because Azure Storage verifies that principal’s required permissions when the SAS is used. Stored access policies and storage account-key regeneration do not revoke a user delegation SAS.

**Learn more:** [Create a user delegation SAS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/create-user-delegation-sas)

finalExplanation: A user delegation SAS can be revoked by revoking its user delegation key, which invalidates SAS tokens signed with that key. It can also be revoked by changing or removing the RBAC role assignment for the security principal used to create the SAS, because Azure Storage verifies that principal’s required permissions when the SAS is used. Stored access policies and storage account-key regeneration do not revoke a user delegation SAS.

definition.stemRaw:
You have two Azure Container Registry (ACR) instances: ACR01 and ACR02.  
  
You plan to implement a containerized application named APP1 that will use a base image named BASE1. The APP1 image will be stored in ACR01, while the BASE1 image will be stored in ACR02.  
  
You need to automate the planned implementation by using five Azure CLI commands. The solution must ensure that the APP1 image in ACR01 is automatically updated when the BASE1 image is updated.  
  
In which order should you perform the actions?  
  
*Note: More than one ordering of the answer choices is correct. You receive credit for any correct order.*

finalExplanation: Following the Microsoft tutorial for triggering an app-image rebuild when a base image in a different registry is updated: first build the base image into ACR02 with 'az acr build'; then create the tracking task in ACR01 with 'az acr task create --assign-identity' (which provisions the task's managed identity); then grant that identity pull rights on ACR02 with 'az role assignment create'; then attach the cross-registry credential to the task with 'az acr task credential add --use-identity [system]'; finally run 'az acr task run' once so the task discovers its base-image dependency. The role assignment must precede the credential add because the credential references the identity that the role grants access to (the note confirms multiple orderings can earn credit, but this is the documented sequence).

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: Include Azure Redis Cache in the design.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Cache for Redis is an in-memory cache whose data resides in the selected Azure region by default. Although supported tiers can provide high availability and geo-replication, an application must explicitly use regional cache instances and route clients to an appropriate endpoint; Redis Cache alone does not provide geographically nearest content delivery for streaming users.

**Learn more:** [Azure Cache for Redis planning FAQs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-planning-faq) · [High availability for Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-high-availability)

finalExplanation: Azure Cache for Redis is an in-memory cache whose data resides in the selected Azure region by default. Although supported tiers can provide high availability and geo-replication, an application must explicitly use regional cache instances and route clients to an appropriate endpoint; Redis Cache alone does not provide geographically nearest content delivery for streaming users.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You add an Azure Content Delivery Network (CDN) to the design.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Content Delivery Network caches publicly available content on edge servers close to end users, reducing latency and origin load. It supports on-demand video streaming and improves delivery performance and availability for geographically distributed users.

**Learn more:** [CDN guidance - Azure Architecture Center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/best-practices/cdn)

finalExplanation: Azure Content Delivery Network caches publicly available content on edge servers close to end users, reducing latency and origin load. It supports on-demand video streaming and improves delivery performance and availability for geographically distributed users.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You incorporate a Storage Area Network (SAN) into your design.

You develop and deploy an Azure Logic app that invokes an Azure Function app. The Azure Function app contains an OpenAPI (Swagger) definition and uses an Azure Blob storage account. All resources are secured by using Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).  
  
The Azure Logic app must securely access the Azure Blob storage account. Azure AD resources must remain if the Azure Logic app is deleted.  
  
You need to secure the Azure Logic app.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a user-assigned managed identity and assign role-based access controls.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an Azure AD custom role and assign the role to the Azure Blob storage account.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Azure Key Vault and issue a client certificate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a system-assigned managed identity and issue a client certificate.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Create an Azure AD custom role and assign role-based access controls.

definition.explanation:
A user-assigned managed identity is independent of the Logic App resource lifecycle, so deleting the Logic App does not automatically delete the identity in Microsoft Entra ID. Assigning the identity an appropriate Azure RBAC role on the Blob storage account grants secure, credential-free access to the storage resource.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate workflow connections to protected Azure resources by using managed identities in Azure Logic Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/logic-apps/authenticate-with-managed-identity) · [Securing managed identities in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/service-accounts-managed-identities)

finalExplanation: A user-assigned managed identity is independent of the Logic App resource lifecycle, so deleting the Logic App does not automatically delete the identity in Microsoft Entra ID. Get-AzSubscription only lists accessible subscriptions and is not required in this sequence.

You manage a data-processing application that receives requests from an Azure Storage queue.  
  
You need to control access to the queue and must meet these requirements:  
  
- Provide other applications with access to the Azure queue.  
- Ensure you can revoke access to the queue without regenerating the storage account keys.  
- Specify access at the queue level rather than at the storage account level.  
  
Which type of shared access signature (SAS) should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Service SAS with a stored access policy

choices.label: D

definition.explanation:
A service SAS can grant permissions to a specific Azure Storage queue. Binding it to a stored access policy on that queue permits access to be revoked or changed centrally by modifying or deleting the policy, without regenerating storage account keys. Stored access policies apply to service-level SAS tokens and are supported for queues.

**Learn more:** [Define a stored access policy - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/define-stored-access-policy) · [Create a service SAS - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/create-service-sas)

finalExplanation: A service SAS can grant permissions to a specific Azure Storage queue. Binding it to a stored access policy on that queue permits access to be revoked or changed centrally by modifying or deleting the policy, without regenerating storage account keys. Stored access policies apply to service-level SAS tokens and are supported for queues.

statements.text: SaveScore will work with Cosmos DB.
SaveScore will update and replace a record if one already exists with the same playerId and gameId.
Leader board data for the game will be automatically partitioned using gameId.
SaveScore will store the values for the gameId and playerId parameters in the database.

definition.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB for Table supports applications written for the Azure Table Storage client surface. A table entity is uniquely identified by its `PartitionKey` and `RowKey`; `Insert` does not replace an existing entity, and partitioning follows the entity partition key rather than automatically following a method argument such as `gameId`. The score entity constructed from the supplied arguments stores the game and player identifiers.

**Learn more:** [Azure Cosmos DB for Table documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/table/) · [Partitioning and horizontal scaling in Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/partitioning)

finalExplanation: Azure Cosmos DB for Table supports applications written for the Azure Table Storage client surface. A table entity is uniquely identified by its `PartitionKey` and `RowKey`; `Insert` does not replace an existing entity, and partitioning follows the entity partition key rather than automatically following a method argument such as `gameId`. The score entity constructed from the supplied arguments stores the game and player identifiers.

definition.stemRaw:
You are building a microservices-based application that uses Azure Container Apps. The application includes several containerized services that perform tasks such as processing orders, managing inventory, and generating reports. You deploy two microservices, named serviceA and serviceB, to support inventory management.  
  
You have the following requirements:  
  
- serviceA and serviceB must publish events to one Azure Event Hub by using the Event Hubs SDK.  
- serviceA must publish 1,000 events per second.  
- serviceB must publish 3,000 events per second.  
- Costs must be minimized.  
  
You need to support event publishing.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create four partitions. Update serviceA to use one partition and serviceB to use three partitions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable and configure Azure Event Hubs Capture.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Azure Event Hubs dedicated cluster. Configure the capacity units to one and the scaling units to two.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create and configure an Azure Schema Registry in Event Hubs. Update serviceA and serviceB to validate message schemas.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Create four consumer groups. Update serviceA to use one consumer group and serviceB to use three consumer groups.

definition.explanation:
Partitions provide parallel publishing paths in an event hub. Allocating one partition to the 1,000-events-per-second publisher and three partitions to the 3,000-events-per-second publisher supplies four parallel publishing paths while avoiding the additional cost and unrelated functionality of a dedicated cluster, Capture, Schema Registry, or consumer groups. In Standard tier, the namespace must also have sufficient throughput units because throughput units control total ingress capacity; each provides up to 1,000 ingress events per second. [Microsoft Learn: Scaling with Event Hubs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-scalability)

**Learn more:** [Scaling with Event Hubs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-scalability) · [Compare Azure Event Hubs tiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/compare-tiers)

finalExplanation: Partitions provide parallel publishing paths in an event hub. Allocating one partition to the 1,000-events-per-second publisher and three partitions to the 3,000-events-per-second publisher supplies four parallel publishing paths while avoiding the additional cost and unrelated functionality of a dedicated cluster, Capture, Schema Registry, or consumer groups. In Standard tier, the namespace must also have sufficient throughput units because throughput units control total ingress capacity; each provides up to 1,000 ingress events per second. [Microsoft Learn: Scaling with Event Hubs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-scalability)

You need to determine the object ID attribute value for each identity.  
  
Which command should you use?
definition.explanation:
For a VM with a system-assigned managed identity, the managed identity's object ID is the resource identity `PrincipalId`. `Get-AzResource` retrieves the VM resource and exposes this value through `Identity.PrincipalId`.

**Learn more:** [Assign a managed identity to an app role using PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/id-id/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/assign-app-role-managed-identity-powershell) · [Get-AzResource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.resources/get-azresource?view=azps-15.6.0&viewFallbackFrom=azps-14.5.0)

finalExplanation: For a VM with a system-assigned managed identity, the managed identity's object ID is the resource identity `PrincipalId`. `Get-AzResource` retrieves the VM resource and exposes this value through `Identity.PrincipalId`.

definition.stemRaw:
You are building several microservices that will run on Azure Container Apps for a company. External TCP ingress traffic from the internet is enabled for the microservices.  
  
The company requires the microservices to scale based on an Azure Event Hub trigger.  
  
You need to scale the microservices by using a custom scaling rule.  
  
Which two Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling (KEDA) trigger fields should you use? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
definition.explanation:
An Azure Container Apps custom scaling rule uses the KEDA scaler `type` to identify the Event Hubs scaler and `metadata` to provide the scaler’s required Event Hubs settings and scaling threshold. Microsoft’s Container Apps scaling documentation maps these KEDA trigger fields to the custom rule’s `type` and `metadata` properties.

**Learn more:** [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app)

finalExplanation: An Azure Container Apps custom scaling rule uses the KEDA scaler `type` to identify the Event Hubs scaler and `metadata` to provide the scaler’s required Event Hubs settings and scaling threshold. Microsoft’s Container Apps scaling documentation maps these KEDA trigger fields to the custom rule’s `type` and `metadata` properties.

definition.stemRaw:
You are building a microservices-based application that uses Azure Container Apps. The application includes several containerized services that perform tasks such as processing orders, managing inventory, and generating reports. You deploy a new revision of the processing orders app.  
  
Processing orders must be triggered by a web request and must always be available in response to incoming web requests.  
  
You need to verify that the replica is ready to handle incoming requests.  
  
What should you implement?
definition.explanation:
An HTTP readiness probe checks whether a replica is ready to receive incoming requests through an HTTP endpoint. Azure Container Apps uses readiness status to determine whether a revision can receive traffic, whereas startup and liveness probes serve different health-check purposes.

**Learn more:** [Health probes in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/health-probes)

finalExplanation: An HTTP readiness probe checks whether a replica is ready to receive incoming requests through an HTTP endpoint. Azure Container Apps uses readiness status to determine whether a revision can receive traffic, whereas startup and liveness probes serve different health-check purposes.

You administer an Azure App Service web app named App1 and its associated Azure Application Insights resource, AppInsights1.  
  
You need alerts for any abnormal increase in the rate of failed HTTP requests directed at App1.  
  
You must implement push notifications.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy an Azure Resource Manager template that configures AppInsights1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From the Azure portal, modify a smart detection rule of AppInsights1.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.text: From the Azure portal, modify an action group of Azure Monitor.

finalExplanation: Application Insights Failure Anomalies detects abnormal increases in failed HTTP request rates. Azure Monitor action groups define alert notification channels and support Azure app push notifications, so the action group associated with the alert must be modified to add the push-notification receiver.

How should network security be configured?

definition.stemRaw:
You have an on-premises, internal-only website named www-contoso.com and an Azure Application Insights instance named AppInsights1.  
  
You need to implement availability testing for www.contoso.com by using AppInsights1. The solution must minimize development effort.  
  
How should you configure the test?
definition.explanation:
The website is internal-only and on-premises, so Application Insights first needs network reachability from Azure into that private network; a Site-to-Site VPN connects the on-premises network to an Azure VNet, letting a VNet-hosted test agent reach the internal site. URL ping tests and Standard tests both run from Microsoft-managed global points of presence and cannot reach a private/internal endpoint, so neither can monitor an internal-only URL. The only option that works is a custom availability test using the TrackAvailability() API, run from code (for example an Azure Function) inside the VNet that can reach the site over the VPN and post results to AppInsights1. Hence Site-to-Site VPN plus a Custom TrackAvailability test.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability)

finalExplanation: The website is internal-only and on-premises, so Application Insights first needs network reachability from Azure into that private network; a Site-to-Site VPN connects the on-premises network to an Azure VNet, letting a VNet-hosted test agent reach the internal site. URL ping tests and Standard tests both run from Microsoft-managed global points of presence and cannot reach a private/internal endpoint, so neither can monitor an internal-only URL. The only option that works is a custom availability test using the TrackAvailability() API, run from code (for example an Azure Function) inside the VNet that can reach the site over the VPN and post results to AppInsights1. Hence Site-to-Site VPN plus a Custom TrackAvailability test.

definition.stemRaw:
You build a web application that sells access to last-minute vacancies at child camps that operate on weekends. The application uses Azure Application Insights for all monitoring and alerting.  
  
The application must notify operators when a technical problem prevents camp sales.  
  
You need to create an alert that detects technical problems.  
  
Which alert type should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Metric alert using multiple time series

choices.label: C
choices.text: Log alert using multiple time series

definition.explanation:
A metric alert with dynamic thresholds is suited to a sales metric whose normal behavior follows a weekend pattern. Dynamic thresholds learn historical metric behavior, including hourly, daily, and weekly patterns, and identify anomalous deviations such as an unexpected drop in sales that can indicate a technical failure. Multiple time series is intended for separately monitoring multiple dimension or resource series, which is not required here.

**Learn more:** [Alert rules with dynamic thresholds overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-dynamic-thresholds) · [Create Azure Monitor metric alert rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-create-metric-alert-rule)

finalExplanation: A metric alert with dynamic thresholds is suited to a sales metric whose normal behavior follows a weekend pattern. Dynamic thresholds learn historical metric behavior, including hourly, daily, and weekly patterns, and identify anomalous deviations such as an unexpected drop in sales that can indicate a technical failure. Multiple time series is intended for separately monitoring multiple dimension or resource series, which is not required here.

definition.stemRaw:
A company uses an Azure Storage static website with a custom domain name.  
  
The company reports that unauthorized users in another country or region are accessing the website. The static website must meet these requirements:  
  
- Unauthorized users must be unable to access the website.  
- Users must be able to access the website over HTTPS.  
  
You need to make the required changes to the static website.

blanks.label: Prevent access from unauthorized users.
blanks.answer: Configure a firewall rule on the storage account.
options: Configure a firewall rule on the storage account.
Configure the public access level of the web container to Blob.
Configure the storage account to use Microsoft Entra ID authentication.
Configure the AllowBlobPublicAccess property for the storage account to False.

blanks.label: Require HTTPS access to the website.
blanks.answer: Enable Azure Content Delivery Network on the storage account.
options: Enable Azure Content Delivery Network on the storage account.
Configure the storage account to require secure transfer.
Configure Azure Traffic Manager for incoming traffic to the website.

finalExplanation: To block users from specific countries/regions you restrict network access with a storage account firewall rule (allowing only permitted IP ranges/networks); this applies to the static-website web endpoint. Setting AllowBlobPublicAccess to False would break the anonymous read that the static website depends on, and Entra ID auth cannot serve anonymous web content, so those are wrong. For HTTPS, the 'require secure transfer' setting only enforces HTTPS on the built-in *.web/*.blob endpoints and does NOT apply to a custom domain name; Azure Storage has no native HTTPS support for custom domains. To serve the custom-domain static site over HTTPS you must front it with Azure CDN (or Azure Front Door), which terminates TLS for the custom domain. That makes the CDN the required choice here.

definition.stemRaw:
You are building a traffic-monitoring system for six highways that produces time-series-analysis reports for each highway.  
  
Traffic-sensor data is stored in Azure Event Hub.  
  
Four departments consume the traffic data. Each department has an Azure Web App that displays the time-series reports and includes a WebJob that processes incoming Event Hub data. All Web Apps run on App Service Plans with three instances.  
  
Data throughput must be maximized and latency minimized.  
  
You need to implement the Azure Event Hub. Which settings should you use?
definition.explanation:
The partition key must be Highway so that all events for a given highway are consistently routed to the same partition, preserving the per-highway ordering that time-series analysis requires. With Highway as the key there are only six distinct key values, so six partitions is the correct count: it gives one dedicated, independently readable channel per highway, maximizing parallel throughput and minimizing latency. Choosing 12 partitions is wrong because six distinct keys can never populate more than six partitions, leaving the extra six permanently empty; the number of departments/instances (4 x 3 = 12) drives consumer-side parallelism, not the partition count, since each department is its own consumer group and can already read all six partitions.

**Learn more:** [Event Hubs features and terminology](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-features) · [Event Hubs scalability](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-scalability)

finalExplanation: The partition key must be Highway so that all events for a given highway are consistently routed to the same partition, preserving the per-highway ordering that time-series analysis requires. With Highway as the key there are only six distinct key values, so six partitions is the correct count: it gives one dedicated, independently readable channel per highway, maximizing parallel throughput and minimizing latency. Choosing 12 partitions is wrong because six distinct keys can never populate more than six partitions, leaving the extra six permanently empty; the number of departments/instances (4 x 3 = 12) drives consumer-side parallelism, not the partition count, since each department is its own consumer group and can already read all six partitions.

definition.stemRaw:
You are building an Azure solution that collects inventory data from thousands of stores worldwide. Each store sends inventory data hourly to an Azure Blob storage account for processing.  
  
The solution must:  
  
- Start processing when data is saved to Azure Blob storage.  
- Filter data by store-location information.  
- Trigger an Azure Logic App to process the data for output to Azure Cosmos DB.  
- Provide high availability and geographic distribution.  
- Permit 24 hours for retries.  
- Use exponential-backoff data processing.  
  
What should you implement?
definition.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage produces blob-created events. Azure Event Grid routes and filters these events, with 24-hour retries and exponential-backoff delivery. Azure Logic App is a supported Event Grid handler and can process the event before writing to Azure Cosmos DB.

**Learn more:** [Azure Event Grid message delivery and retry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/delivery-and-retry) · [Reacting to Azure Blob storage events](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-event-overview)

finalExplanation: Azure Blob Storage produces blob-created events. Azure Event Grid routes and filters these events, with 24-hour retries and exponential-backoff delivery. Azure Logic App is a supported Event Grid handler and can process the event before writing to Azure Cosmos DB.

You have an Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL API account named account1. Multiple instances of an on-premises application named app1 read data from account1.  
  
You plan to implement integrated cache for connections from the instances of app1 to account1.  
  
You need to configure the connection mode and maximum consistency level for app1.  
  
Which values should you use for the configuration settings?
definition.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB integrated cache runs on the dedicated gateway and requires connections in gateway mode using the dedicated gateway. It supports session and eventual consistency; strong consistency reads bypass the cache. Therefore, session is the highest supported consistency level.

**Learn more:** [Azure Cosmos DB integrated cache overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/integrated-cache)

finalExplanation: Azure Cosmos DB integrated cache runs on the dedicated gateway and requires connections in gateway mode using the dedicated gateway. It supports session and eventual consistency; strong consistency reads bypass the cache. Therefore, session is the highest supported consistency level.

The solution must receive and retain messages until they can be processed. You create an Azure Service Bus instance by specifying a name, pricing tier, subscription, resource group, and location.  
  
You need to finish the configuration.

Run the following command at an elevated command prompt:

definition.stemRaw:
A software as a service (SaaS) company delivers document-management services. The company has a service consisting of several Azure web apps. All Azure web apps run in an Azure App Service plan named `PrimaryASP`.  
  
You are developing a new web service that uses a web app named `ExcelParser`. The web app contains a third-party library for processing Microsoft Excel files. The library license stipulates that only a single instance of the library can run.  
  
You need to configure the service. How should you complete the script?
definition.template:
Set-AzAppServicePlan `
    -ResourceGroupName $rg `
    -Name “PrimaryASP” `
    {{plan_setting}}

$app = Get-AzWebApp `
    -ResourceGroupName $rg `
    -Name “ExcelParser”
$app.{{app_setting}}

Set-AzWebApp $app
definition.explanation:
Per-app scaling must be enabled on the App Service plan by setting `PerSiteScaling` to true. The per-app instance count is controlled by `SiteConfig.NumberOfWorkers`, so setting it to 1 limits ExcelParser to one worker instance without limiting the other web apps in the shared plan.

**Learn more:** [Per-App Scaling for High-Density Hosting - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/app-service/manage-scale-per-app) · [Set-AzAppServicePlan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.websites/set-azappserviceplan?view=azps-15.3.0)

finalExplanation: Per-app scaling must be enabled on the App Service plan by setting `PerSiteScaling` to true. The per-app instance count is controlled by `SiteConfig.NumberOfWorkers`, so setting it to 1 limits ExcelParser to one worker instance without limiting the other web apps in the shared plan.

definition.stemRaw:
You develop and deploy an ASP.NET Core application that connects to an Azure Database for MySQL instance.  
  
Database connections seem to drop intermittently, and the application code does not handle connection failures.  
  
You need to handle transient connection errors in code by implementing retries.  
  
What are three possible ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Close the database connection and immediately report an error.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable connection pooling and configure a second Azure Database for MySQL instance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wait five seconds before repeating the connection attempt to the database.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set a maximum number of connection attempts to 10 and report an error on subsequent connections.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increase connection repeat attempts exponentially up to 120 seconds.

definition.explanation:
Transient Azure Database for MySQL connectivity failures should use retry logic that waits before the initial retry, increases retry delays exponentially when failures persist, and limits the number of retries before treating the operation as failed. This prevents immediate repeated requests during recovery while ensuring the application does not retry indefinitely.

**Learn more:** [Architecture Best Practices for Azure Database for MySQL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/service-guides/azure-database-for-mysql) · [Transient Fault Handling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/best-practices/transient-faults)

finalExplanation: Transient Azure Database for MySQL connectivity failures should use retry logic that waits before the initial retry, increases retry delays exponentially when failures persist, and limits the number of retries before treating the operation as failed. This prevents immediate repeated requests during recovery while ensuring the application does not retry indefinitely.

Update the app to meet these requirements:  
  
- Use the `Export` feature in the app without restarting the app.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Use dynamic configuration in an ASP.NET Core app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-app-configuration/enable-dynamic-configuration-aspnet-core) · [ASP.NET Core middleware](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/middleware/)

finalExplanation: `UseAzureAppConfiguration` adds Azure App Configuration’s request-driven refresh middleware, allowing feature-flag values to refresh without restarting the application. Authentication must run before authorization: it creates the authenticated user principal, and authorization then evaluates whether that user may access protected resources.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure Queue Storage account containing a queue named `queue1`.  
  
You plan to use the Azure SDK for .NET to develop a solution that uses `queue1`.  
  
You need to write C# code that returns an approximate count of the messages in `queue1`. The solution must minimize development effort.  
  
Which method should you use in your code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: GetProperties method of the QueueClient class

choices.label: B
choices.text: GetProperties method of the QueueServiceClient class

choices.label: C
choices.text: PeekMessages method of the QueueClient class

choices.label: D
choices.text: GetStatistics method of the QueueServiceClient class

definition.explanation:
`QueueClient.GetProperties` retrieves the properties of a specific queue, and the returned `QueueProperties.ApproximateMessagesCount` value provides the queue's approximate message count. This is the direct SDK operation for obtaining the estimate without retrieving messages.

**Learn more:** [Quickstart: Azure Queue Storage client library for .NET](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/queues/storage-quickstart-queues-dotnet) · [QueueClient.GetProperties Method (Azure.Storage.Queues)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/azure.storage.queues.queueclient.getproperties?view=azure-dotnet)

finalExplanation: `QueueClient.GetProperties` retrieves the properties of a specific queue, and the returned `QueueProperties.ApproximateMessagesCount` value provides the queue's approximate message count. This is the direct SDK operation for obtaining the estimate without retrieving messages.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You configure Basic gateway credentials for the HTTP(S) endpoint.  
  
Does this solution satisfy the goal?

You develop a web application that provides access to legal documents stored in Azure Blob Storage using version-level immutability policies. The documents are protected by both time-based policies and legal-hold policies. Every time-based retention policy has the `AllowProtectedAppendWrites` property enabled.  
  
You must prevent users from attempting operations that would fail only if a legal hold is active and all other policies have expired.  
  
You need to meet the requirement.  
  
Which two operations should you prevent? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
definition.explanation:
With version-level immutability, overwriting a blob creates a new version, so an existing version’s legal hold does not block the overwrite. New blobs can also be created. `AllowProtectedAppendWrites` permits appending while a time-based retention policy is active; after that policy expires, an active legal hold prevents modifying the held document, including adding data. A legal hold also prevents deletion until it is explicitly cleared.

**Learn more:** [Version-level WORM policies for immutable blob data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-version-level-worm-policies) · [Store business-critical blob data with immutable storage in a WORM state](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-storage-overview)

finalExplanation: With version-level immutability, overwriting a blob creates a new version, so an existing version’s legal hold does not block the overwrite. New blobs can also be created. `AllowProtectedAppendWrites` permits appending while a time-based retention policy is active; after that policy expires, an active legal hold prevents modifying the held document, including adding data. A legal hold also prevents deletion until it is explicitly cleared.

You are preparing to deploy an Azure virtual machine (VM)-based application.  
  
The application VMs have these requirements:  
  
- When a VM is provisioned, its firewall must be automatically configured before it can access Azure resources.  
- Supporting services must be installed by using an Azure PowerShell script stored in Azure Storage.  
  
You need to ensure the requirements are met. Which features should you use?  
  
Each feature may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
definition.explanation:
The Custom Script Extension runs automatically during VM provisioning, so it can configure the firewall before the VM accesses Azure resources, and it can download and run a PowerShell script directly from Azure Storage to install the supporting services — satisfying both requirements. Serial console is an interactive troubleshooting tool that requires manual connection and cannot run automatically at provisioning, so it is incorrect for the firewall action. Run Command is for on-demand ad hoc execution, and Hybrid Runbook Worker targets on-premises/hybrid Automation scenarios, neither of which fits automatic post-provisioning configuration from a stored script.

**Learn more:** [Azure Custom Script Extension for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/extensions/custom-script-windows)

finalExplanation: The Custom Script Extension runs automatically during VM provisioning, so it can configure the firewall before the VM accesses Azure resources, and it can download and run a PowerShell script directly from Azure Storage to install the supporting services — satisfying both requirements. Serial console is an interactive troubleshooting tool that requires manual connection and cannot run automatically at provisioning, so it is incorrect for the firewall action. Run Command is for on-demand ad hoc execution, and Hybrid Runbook Worker targets on-premises/hybrid Automation scenarios, neither of which fits automatic post-provisioning configuration from a stored script.

A dead-letter queue records documents that cannot be processed, allowing the processing callback to complete so the change feed processor can checkpoint and continue to later batches. Life-cycle notifications provide handlers such as `WithErrorNotification` for processor and delegate errors. A lease container maintains checkpoint and coordination state; the change feed estimator only measures outstanding work.

**Learn more:** [Read Change Feed - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/read-change-feed) · [Change Feed Processor - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/change-feed-processor)

finalExplanation: A dead-letter queue records documents that cannot be processed, allowing the processing callback to complete so the change feed processor can checkpoint and continue to later batches. Life-cycle notifications provide handlers such as `WithErrorNotification` for processor and delegate errors. A lease container maintains checkpoint and coordination state; the change feed estimator only measures outstanding work.

You use Azure Front Door Service and expect inbound files to use Brotli compression. You find that inbound XML files, each 9 MB in size, are not compressed.

statements.text: The file MIME type is supported by the service.
Edge nodes must be purged of all cache assets.

definition.explanation:
Azure Front Door supports XML MIME types and Brotli compression. However, a file must be smaller than 8 MB to qualify for compression, so a 9 MB XML file is not eligible. Cache purging only removes cached assets and does not make an oversized file compressible.

An endpoint that runs the required scripts and returns an accepted status code ensures those actions complete before the swap proceeds.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: Turn on auto swap for the Testing slot. Deploy the app to the Testing slot.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
Auto swap warms the source slot before swapping, but enabling it does not configure custom initialization actions. For Windows-hosted Azure App Service apps, the `applicationInitialization` element in `Web.config` specifies custom warm-up actions, and App Service waits for that warm-up to finish before swapping with the target slot.

You are developing several APIs hosted in Azure API Management (APIM).  
  
You must inspect API request processing in APIM, including requests made to APIM by using a REST client. The request inspection must include the following information:  
  
- Requests APIM sent to the API backend and the response that it received  
- Policies applied to the response before it is returned to the caller  
- Errors that occurred while processing the request and the policies applied to those errors  
- The original request APIM received from the caller and the policies applied to the request  
  
You need to inspect the APIs.  
  
Which three actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable the Allow tracing setting for the subscription used to inspect the API.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add the Ocp-Apim-Trace header value to the API call whit a value set to true.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header value to the key for a subscription that allows access to the API.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create and configure a custom policy. Apply the policy to the inbound policy section with a global scope.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Create and configure a custom policy. Apply the policy to the outbound policy section with an API scope.

definition.explanation:
In the legacy subscription-based APIM tracing model, complete request traces are enabled by allowing tracing on the subscription, sending `Ocp-Apim-Trace: true`, and including an `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key` for a subscription that can access the API. The built-in trace records inbound, backend, outbound, and error processing, including policy execution; custom inbound or outbound policies are not required. Current APIM documentation notes that this legacy subscription/header mechanism is no longer supported and has been replaced by time-limited API-level trace tokens.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Debug APIs in Azure API Management using request tracing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-howto-api-inspector) · [Azure API Management policy reference - trace](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/trace-policy)

The built-in trace records inbound, backend, outbound, and error processing, including policy execution; custom inbound or outbound policies are not required. Current APIM documentation notes that this legacy subscription/header mechanism is no longer supported and has been replaced by time-limited API-level trace tokens.

definition.explanation:
Storing an image in its native format relies on a system property — specifically the Content-Type (ContentType) system property — which tells clients and browsers the correct MIME type so the image renders in its native format. Arbitrary application data such as a photo's EXIF information is stored as user-defined metadata, which are custom name-value pairs attached to the blob for your own purposes. Index tags would be used if you needed native, indexed search/classification across blobs, and Change feed is an ordered log of blob change events — neither is used to store the image bytes' format or EXIF data.

Arbitrary application data such as a photo's EXIF information is stored as user-defined metadata, which are custom name-value pairs attached to the blob for your own purposes. Index tags would be used if you needed native, indexed search/classification across blobs, and Change feed is an ordered log of blob change events — neither is used to store the image bytes' format or EXIF data.

definition.stemRaw:
You need to mitigate the Azure Cache for Redis issue.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Test application code by rebooting all nodes in the test environment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure client connections to retry commands with exponential backoff.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Modify the maxmemory policy to evict the least frequently used keys out of all keys.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the maxmemory-reserved and maxfragmentationmemory-reserved values.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Test application code by purging the cache in the test environment.

definition.stemRaw:
You need to implement code that processes inventory changes and updates orders.  
  
Which configuration should you use?

blanks.label: Compute host
options: REST API hosted in Azure App Service
Process in an instance of Azure Virtual Machines
Continuous running instance of WebJobs in Azure App Service

blanks.label: Read Azure Cosmos DB change feed

definition.explanation:
An Azure Functions serverless function is the simplest event-driven compute host for reacting to inventory changes and updating orders, so the compute-host choice is correct. When reading the Azure Cosmos DB change feed, there are two approaches: the pull model, where your client polls and manages its own lease/checkpoint state, and the push model, where the change feed processor pushes new events to your code. The Azure Functions Cosmos DB trigger is built on the change feed processor and therefore uses the PUSH model - the function is automatically invoked on each new change. Because the compute host is an Azure Function, the matching change-feed read mechanism is the push model, not the pull model.

**Learn more:** [Read the Azure Cosmos DB change feed](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/nosql/read-change-feed) · [Change feed with Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/change-feed-functions)

finalExplanation: An Azure Functions serverless function is the simplest event-driven compute host for reacting to inventory changes and updating orders, so the compute-host choice is correct. When reading the Azure Cosmos DB change feed, there are two approaches: the pull model, where your client polls and manages its own lease/checkpoint state, and the push model, where the change feed processor pushes new events to your code. The Azure Functions Cosmos DB trigger is built on the change feed processor and therefore uses the PUSH model - the function is automatically invoked on each new change. Because the compute host is an Azure Function, the matching change-feed read mechanism is the push model, not the pull model.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a SQL role definition under the Azure Cosmas DB account.Assign the role to the function apps system-assigned managed identity.Programmatically access the Azure Cosmos DB keys from the function app.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing an application that stores business-critical data in Azure Blob storage.  
  
The application must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- Data must not be changed or deleted for a user-specified interval.  
- Data must be safeguarded against overwrites and deletions.  
- Data must be written once and readable many times.  
  
You need to protect the data in the Azure Blob storage account.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure a time-based retention policy for the storage account.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable the blob change feed for the storage account.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable version-level immutability support for the storage account.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enable point-in-time restore for containers in the storage account.

definition.explanation:
Azure Blob immutable storage supports a write-once, read-many (WORM) state. A time-based retention policy prevents protected blob data from being modified or deleted for the configured retention interval. Version-level immutability support must be enabled before a default version-level time-based retention policy can be configured for a storage account.

**Learn more:** [Configure immutability policies for blob versions - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-policy-configure-version-scope) · [Version-level WORM policies for immutable blob data - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-version-level-worm-policies)

finalExplanation: Azure Blob immutable storage supports a write-once, read-many (WORM) state. A time-based retention policy prevents protected blob data from being modified or deleted for the configured retention interval. Version-level immutability support must be enabled before a default version-level time-based retention policy can be configured for a storage account.

You need to construct the GET request URI.  
  
Each parameter may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
definition.template: https://{{account}}.blob.core.windows.net/{{container}}?restype=container&comp=blobs&where={{expression}}
definition.explanation:
The container-scoped Find Blobs by Tags operation places the storage account in the host name and the container in the path, then uses `restype=container&comp=blobs`. Its `where` parameter accepts an equality expression; `Status ='Final'` selects blobs whose Status tag equals Final. The expression must be URI encoded in an actual HTTP request.

**Learn more:** [Find Blobs by Tags in Container (REST API)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/find-blobs-by-tags-container)

finalExplanation: The container-scoped Find Blobs by Tags operation places the storage account in the host name and the container in the path, then uses `restype=container&comp=blobs`. Its `where` parameter accepts an equality expression; `Status ='Final'` selects blobs whose Status tag equals Final. The expression must be URI encoded in an actual HTTP request.

The validation request contains the `WebHook-Request-Origin` header, and the webhook must recognize it and respond with an appropriate `WebHook-Allowed-Origin` value. A CDN in front of the Azure Function must therefore allow `WebHook-Request-Origin` to pass through.

- Support alternative input parameters.

slots.label: Provide additional context to back-end services.

definition.explanation:
Inbound policies modify an incoming request before it is sent to the backend, including rewriting a public URL or query parameters into the form expected by the service. Outbound policies modify the backend response before it is sent to the caller, which is where response formatting can be removed. Backend policies run immediately before forwarding the request to the backend service and can add or otherwise supply context for that service.

**Learn more:** [Azure API Management policy reference – Rewrite URL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/rewrite-uri-policy) · [Set or edit Azure API Management policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/set-edit-policies)

Outbound policies modify the backend response before it is sent to the caller, which is where response formatting can be removed. Backend policies run immediately before forwarding the request to the backend service and can add or otherwise supply context for that service.

You are developing an Azure Function that connects to an Azure SQL Database instance. The function is triggered by an Azure Storage queue.  
  
You receive reports of numerous `System.InvalidOperationExceptions` with the following message:  
  
`Timeout expired. The timeout period elapsed prior to obtaining a connection from the pool. This may have occurred because all pooled connections were in use and max pool size was reached.`  
  
You need to prevent this exception. What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the host.json file, decrease the value of the batchSize option

choices.label: B
choices.text: Convert the trigger to Azure Event Hub

choices.label: C
choices.text: Convert the Azure Function to the Premium plan

choices.label: D

definition.explanation:
An Azure Storage queue trigger retrieves and processes queue messages concurrently. The `batchSize` setting in `host.json` controls the number of messages processed in parallel, so decreasing it reduces concurrent Azure Function invocations and their simultaneous Azure SQL Database connection usage. This avoids exhausting the SQL connection pool.

**Learn more:** [Azure Queue storage trigger and bindings for Azure Functions overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-storage-queue)

The `batchSize` setting in `host.json` controls the number of messages processed in parallel, so decreasing it reduces concurrent Azure Function invocations and their simultaneous Azure SQL Database connection usage. This avoids exhausting the SQL connection pool.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing a microservices-based application by using Azure Container Apps. The application includes several containerized services that perform tasks such as processing orders, managing inventory, and generating reports.  
  
Order processing has these requirements:  
  
- Orders must be triggered by a web request.  
- Additional replicas must be added when the total web-request count exceeds 300 for at least 15 seconds.  
- Order processing must remain available according to incoming web requests.  
- Costs for the Azure Container Apps instance must be minimized.  
  
You need to configure scaling.  
  
How should you complete the CLI command?
definition.template:
az containerapp {{command}} \
  --name OrderProcessingApp \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --environment MyEnvironmentName \
  --image myimage:latest \
  --min-replicas {{min_replicas}} \
  --max-replicas 10 \
  --scale-rule-name azure-http-rule \
  --scale-rule-type http \
  --scale-rule-http-concurrency 20
definition.explanation:
`az containerapp create` deploys the Container App. An HTTP scale rule evaluates requests in 15-second intervals, so 300 requests over 15 seconds corresponds to the configured target of 20 requests per second. With HTTP ingress and an HTTP scale rule, Azure Container Apps can activate from zero replicas when requests arrive. Thus, `--min-replicas 0` minimizes idle cost while retaining request-driven scaling.

**Learn more:** [Scaling in Azure Container Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-apps/scale-app) · [az containerapp create](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/containerapp?view=azure-cli-latest#az-containerapp-create)

finalExplanation: `az containerapp create` deploys the Container App. An HTTP scale rule evaluates requests in 15-second intervals, so 300 requests over 15 seconds corresponds to the configured target of 20 requests per second. With HTTP ingress and an HTTP scale rule, Azure Container Apps can activate from zero replicas when requests arrive. Thus, `--min-replicas 0` minimizes idle cost while retaining request-driven scaling.

You are creating a loyalty program for a large snack manufacturer. When customers purchase a snack at any of 100 participating retailers, the event is recorded in Azure Event Hub. Each retailer receives a unique identifier that serves as the primary identifier for the loyalty program.  
  
Retailers must be able to be added or removed at any time. A retailer must be able to record sales only for itself.  
  
You need to ensure that retailers can record sales.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a partition for each retailer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Define a namespace for each retailer.

definition.explanation:
Azure Event Hubs publisher policies provide granular control for many independent publishers. Each publisher uses a unique identifier, and the publisher name must match the SAS token used for authentication; consequently, assigning each retailer its identifier as its publisher identity restricts it to publishing its own sales. Partitions organize event streams and namespaces provide broader resource scoping, neither of which enforces publisher-specific sending rights.

**Learn more:** [Event Hubs features and terminology - Azure Event Hubs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-sg/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-features) · [Publisher policy operations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/eventhub/publisher-policy-operations)

finalExplanation: Azure Event Hubs publisher policies provide granular control for many independent publishers. Each publisher uses a unique identifier, and the publisher name must match the SAS token used for authentication; consequently, assigning each retailer its identifier as its publisher identity restricts it to publishing its own sales. Partitions organize event streams and namespaces provide broader resource scoping, neither of which enforces publisher-specific sending rights.

You are developing an Azure Cosmos DB solution using the Azure Cosmos DB SQL API. The data contains millions of documents, and each document can contain hundreds of properties.  
  
The document properties do not have distinct values suitable for partitioning. Azure Cosmos DB must scale individual containers in the database to satisfy the application's performance requirements by distributing the workload evenly across all partitions over time.  
  
You need to choose a partition key.  
  
Which two partition keys can you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: a single property value that does not appear frequently in the documents

choices.label: B
choices.text: a value containing the collection name

choices.label: C
choices.text: a single property value that appears frequently in the documents

choices.label: D
choices.text: a concatenation of multiple property values with a random suffix appended

choices.label: E
choices.text: a hash suffix appended to a property value

definition.explanation:
Synthetic partition keys provide adequate cardinality and distribution when no single property is sufficiently distinct. Concatenating multiple property values with a random suffix spreads writes across partition-key values, and appending a calculated hash suffix similarly distributes workload while allowing the suffix to be reproduced for targeted reads.

**Learn more:** [Create a synthetic partition key - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/synthetic-partition-keys) · [Partitioning and horizontal scaling - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/partitioning)

finalExplanation: Synthetic partition keys provide adequate cardinality and distribution when no single property is sufficiently distinct. Concatenating multiple property values with a random suffix spreads writes across partition-key values, and appending a calculated hash suffix similarly distributes workload while allowing the suffix to be reproduced for targeted reads.
