You develop software solutions for a mobile delivery service. You are building a mobile app that lets users place orders from a restaurant in their area. The app follows this workflow:  
  
1. A driver chooses the restaurants for which they will deliver orders.  
2. Orders are sent to every available driver in an area.  
3. A driver sees only orders for the restaurants they selected.  
4. When the first driver accepts an order, it is removed from the available-orders list.  
  
You need to implement an Azure Service Bus solution.  
  
Which three actions should you perform, in order?

slots.answer: Create s single Service Bus Namespace.
Create a Service Bus topic for each restaurant for which a driver can receive messages.
Create a Service Bus subscription for each restaurant for which a driver can receive orders.

items: Create a single Service Bus topic.
Create a Service Bus Namespace for each restaurant for which a driver can receive messages.
Create a single Service Bus subscription.
Create a Service Bus subscription for each restaurant for which a driver can receive orders.
Create s single Service Bus Namespace.
Create a Service Bus topic for each restaurant for which a driver can receive messages.
definition.explanation:
An Azure Service Bus namespace is the container for Service Bus entities. A topic supports publishing to multiple consumers, and separate restaurant topics isolate each restaurant’s order stream. Creating a subscription for every restaurant a driver selected gives that driver access only to the applicable restaurant order streams.

**Learn more:** [Azure Service Bus messaging overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview) · [Topics, subscriptions, and rules in Azure Service Bus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/topic-filters)

finalExplanation: An Azure Service Bus namespace is the container for Service Bus entities. A topic supports publishing to multiple consumers, and separate restaurant topics isolate each restaurant’s order stream. Creating a subscription for every restaurant a driver selected gives that driver access only to the applicable restaurant order streams.

You are implementing an Azure solution that uses Azure Cosmos DB and the latest Azure Cosmos DB SDK. You add a change feed processor to a new container instance.  
  
You try to read a batch of 100 documents. Processing fails while reading one document. The solution must monitor the progress of the change feed processor instance on the new container as the change feed is read. It must also prevent the processor from retrying the entire batch when a document cannot be read.  
  
Which features should you use? Each feature may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

slots.label: Monitor the progress of the change feed processor
Prevent the change feed processor from retrying the entire batch when one document cannot be read

definition.explanation:
The change feed estimator monitors a processor's progress by estimating the changes pending in the feed. A dead-letter queue persists an individual document that cannot be processed, allowing the processor to continue and avoid becoming stuck retrying the same batch. A lease container stores checkpoint/lease state, while a deployment unit describes a group of processor instances.

**Learn more:** [Use the Change Feed Estimator - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/nosql/how-to-use-change-feed-estimator) · [Change Feed Processor - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/change-feed-processor)

finalExplanation: The change feed estimator monitors a processor's progress by estimating the changes pending in the feed. A dead-letter queue persists an individual document that cannot be processed, allowing the processor to continue and avoid becoming stuck retrying the same batch. A lease container stores checkpoint/lease state, while a deployment unit describes a group of processor instances.

You need to configure the Function App.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use an App Service plan. Configure the Function App to use an Azure Blob Storage input trigger.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a Consumption plan. Configure the Function App to use an Azure Blob Storage trigger.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a Consumption plan. Configure the Function App to use a Timer trigger.

choices.label: D

Blob-trigger processing on a Consumption plan can be delayed when the app has gone idle. An App Service plan can use Always On to avoid that idle delay, making it the appropriate listed plan for low-latency image processing.

**Learn more:** [Azure Blob storage trigger for Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-storage-blob-trigger)

finalExplanation: A Blob Storage trigger runs a function in response to a new or updated blob, whereas a Blob Storage input binding only supplies blob data to a function that has already been invoked. Blob-trigger processing on a Consumption plan can be delayed when the app has gone idle. An App Service plan can use Always On to avoid that idle delay, making it the appropriate listed plan for low-latency image processing.

You have a workspace-based Azure Application Insights resource named Insights1 and an Azure App Service web app named App1. Insights1 collects telemetry produced by App1.  
  
You plan to evaluate the alerting capability of the availability testing enabled for App1 by taking it offline for 50 minutes.  
  
You create a standard availability test for App1, configure its frequency as 15 minutes, and set its alert status to Enabled.  
  
You need to determine how many alerts to expect when App1 is offline for 50 minutes.  
  
How many alerts should you expect?
definition.explanation:
Application Insights availability alerts are state-based: one alert is generated when the endpoint is detected as unavailable, and no further alerts are generated at later evaluations while it remains unavailable. A 15-minute test frequency does not cause repeated alerts during the same 50-minute outage.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability)

finalExplanation: Application Insights availability alerts are state-based: one alert is generated when the endpoint is detected as unavailable, and no further alerts are generated at later evaluations while it remains unavailable. A 15-minute test frequency does not cause repeated alerts during the same 50-minute outage.

definition.stemRaw:
You need to retrieve all order line items from Order.json and sort the results alphabetically by city.  
  
How should you complete the code? Select the appropriate option for each blank in the answer area.

finalExplanation: In Azure Cosmos DB's SQL API, JOIN performs an intra-document self-join that flattens an array property nested inside each item, using the pattern FROM <container> <alias> JOIN <newAlias> IN <alias>.<arrayProperty>. Because the SELECT list projects li.id and li.price, 'li' must be the alias introduced by the JOIN over the order's line_items array, so the query reads FROM Orders o JOIN li IN o.line_items — this produces one output row per line item across all orders. The city value used for sorting belongs to the order's address, which is a property of the order document itself (o.address.city), not of an individual line item, since line items in this data model do not contain an address/city field. Consequently ORDER BY o.address.city ASC correctly sorts the flattened line-item rows alphabetically by the order's city.

Azure Monitor metrics (C) retains data for a limited window and is not suited to per-month historical analysis, and Application Insights alerts (B) only notify on conditions rather than analyze uptime, so each is an incomplete solution.

**Learn more:** [Application Insights availability tests](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/app/availability)

finalExplanation: To analyze monthly uptime you need availability data plus a way to query it over time. Application Insights availability (web/URL ping) tests (D) actively probe the app from multiple locations and record availability results, which is the standard mechanism for measuring uptime of a Traffic Manager-fronted, multi-region app. Azure Monitor Logs (A) stores those availabilityResults and lets you run KQL queries to aggregate uptime per month. Azure Monitor metrics (C) retains data for a limited window and is not suited to per-month historical analysis, and Application Insights alerts (B) only notify on conditions rather than analyze uptime, so each is an incomplete solution.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing an application that transfers data between on-premises file servers and Azure Blob storage. The application stores keys, secrets, and certificates in Azure Key Vault and uses the Azure Key Vault APIs.  
  
You need to configure the application so that an accidentally deleted key vault or key vault object can be recovered for 90 days after deletion.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run the az keyvault update --enable-soft-delete true --enable-purge-protection true CLI.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implement virtual network service endpoints for Azure Key Vault.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run the az keyvault update --enable-soft-delete false CLI.

definition.explanation:
Azure Key Vault soft delete retains deleted vaults and vault objects for a recoverable retention period, which defaults to 90 days. Purge protection prevents permanent purging during that period. Enabling both features provides recovery protection for accidentally deleted vaults, keys, secrets, and certificates.

**Learn more:** [Azure Key Vault recovery management with soft delete and purge protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/key-vault-recovery) · [Azure CLI: az keyvault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/keyvault?view=azure-cli-latest)

finalExplanation: Azure Key Vault soft delete retains deleted vaults and vault objects for a recoverable retention period, which defaults to 90 days. choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure Azure Redis with AOF persistence.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure second storage account for persistence.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set backup frequency to the minimum value.

definition.explanation:
AOF persistence saves every cache write operation to an append-only log and persists that log once per second, providing substantially lower potential data loss than scheduled RDB snapshots. finalExplanation: AOF persistence saves every cache write operation to an append-only log and persists that log once per second, providing substantially lower potential data loss than scheduled RDB snapshots. Change the storage account access tier from hot to cool

Create a new GPv2 Standard account and set its default access tier level to cool
Change the storage account access tier from hot to cool

definition.explanation:
GPv1 accounts do not support blob tiering or lifecycle management, while GPv2 supports these capabilities. Archive storage requires a Standard GPv2 account, so data to be archived is copied there and removed from the Premium source. The cool account tier is appropriate for data that is rarely accessed after three months; archive tiering is then performed per blob by lifecycle management.

Archive storage requires a Standard GPv2 account, so data to be archived is copied there and removed from the Premium source. The cool account tier is appropriate for data that is rarely accessed after three months; archive tiering is then performed per blob by lifecycle management.

You are developing an application that uses a premium block blob storage account. The application processes a large volume of transactions each day, and Blob storage versioning is enabled.  
  
To optimize costs by automating Azure Blob Storage access tiers, you apply the following policy rules to the storage account. (Line numbers are included only for reference.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783809794075-17bl12zq.png)  
  
For each statement, select **Yes** if it is true. Otherwise, select **No**.

statements.text: Block blobs prefixed with transactions will transition blobs that have not been modified in over 60 days to cool storage, and delete blobs not modified in 365 days
Blobs are moved to cool storage if they have not been accessed for 60 days
The policy rule tiers previous versions within a container named transactions that are 60 days or older to the cool tier and deletes previous versions that are 365 days or older
Blobs will automatically be tiered from cool back to hot if accessed again after being tiered to cool

definition.explanation:
`version` lifecycle actions apply to previous versions, and `daysAfterCreationGreaterThan` measures creation age rather than modification or access inactivity. A `prefixMatch` filter is not a declaration of a container named `transactions`. Automatic cool-to-hot tiering requires the explicit `enableAutoTierToHotFromCool` setting and a last-access-time condition. Tiering to cool is also unsupported for premium block blob storage accounts.

**Learn more:** [Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management policy structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-policy-structure) · [Lifecycle management policies that transition blobs between tiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-policy-access-tiers)

finalExplanation: `version` lifecycle actions apply to previous versions, and `daysAfterCreationGreaterThan` measures creation age rather than modification or access inactivity. Tiering to cool is also unsupported for premium block blob storage accounts.

definition.explanation:

A company uses Azure Blob Storage for archiving.  
  
The company requires that data in Blob Storage reside only in the archive tier.  
  
You need to ensure that data copied to Blob Storage is moved to the archive tier.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use a Put Block List operation with a request header of x-ms-immutability-policy-mode.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a lifecycle policy with an action of tierToArchive and configure daysAfterModificationGreaterThan for 0.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a Put Blob operation with a request header of x-ms-immutability-policy-until-date.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a lifecycle policy with an action of tierToArchive and configure a filter for blobIndexMatch.

definition.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management can transition eligible block blobs to the archive access tier through the `tierToArchive` action. Setting `daysAfterModificationGreaterThan` to `0` makes blobs eligible immediately after their last modification, which includes copying data into Blob Storage. Immutability-policy headers do not set an access tier, and a blob-index filter only determines which blobs a lifecycle rule targets.

**Learn more:** [Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management policy structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-policy-structure) · [Lifecycle management policies that transition blobs between tiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/lifecycle-management-policy-access-tiers)

finalExplanation: Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management can transition eligible block blobs to the archive access tier through the `tierToArchive` action. Setting `daysAfterModificationGreaterThan` to `0` makes blobs eligible immediately after their last modification, which includes copying data into Blob Storage. Immutability-policy headers do not set an access tier, and a blob-index filter only determines which blobs a lifecycle rule targets.

You are building a .NET web application that stores data in Azure Cosmos DB. The application must use the Core API and support millions of read and write operations.  
  
The Azure Cosmos DB account was created with multiple write regions enabled. The application is deployed in the East US2 and Central US regions.

Which two actions could accomplish this goal? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Update the ConnectionPolicy class for the Cosmos client and populate the PreferredLocations property based on the geo-proximity of the application.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Update Azure Cosmos DB to use the Strong consistency level. Add indexed properties to the container to indicate region.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Update the ConnectionPolicy class for the Cosmos client and set the UseMultipleWriteLocations property to true.

choices.label: D

Application Insights Profiler captures call stacks for slow requests and stores the results in Application Insights, enabling analysis across App Service instances. Profiler is supported on the Basic App Service tier or higher, so a Premium upgrade is unnecessary and adds cost.

You are developing a solution that uses several Azure Service Bus queues. You create an Azure Event Grid subscription for the Azure Service Bus namespace and use Azure Functions as subscribers to process messages.

The Service Bus-to-Event Grid integration (emitting events such as ActiveMessagesAvailableWithNoListeners) is only available on the Premium namespace tier; Basic and Standard cannot emit events to Event Grid, so Premium is required. Data Receiver is wrong because it only grants the right to receive messages from a queue/subscription, not to configure the namespace's Event Grid integration.

**Learn more:** [Service Bus to Event Grid integration overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-to-event-grid-integration-concept)

Microsoft's documentation explicitly states that to enable this feature you need Contributor access to the Service Bus namespace, and there is no finer-grained built-in role that can create the Event Grid subscription on the namespace, so Contributor is the least-privilege option that can actually perform the task. A development team is building a new REST API that will store data in Azure Blob storage. You plan to deploy the API to Azure App Service.  
  
Developers need access to the Azure Blob storage account to develop the API for the next two months. After that two-month period, the developers must no longer be able to access the Azure Blob storage account.  
  
You need to provide developers access to the Azure Blob storage account.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Generate a shared access signature (SAS) for the Azure Blob storage account and provide the SAS to all developers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create and apply a new lifecycle management policy to include a last accessed date value. Apply the policy to the Azure Blob storage account.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Provide all developers with the access key for the Azure Blob storage account. Update the API to include the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) timestamp for the request header.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Grant all developers access to the Azure Blob storage account by assigning role-based access control (RBAC) roles.

definition.explanation:
A shared access signature (SAS) delegates restricted access to Azure Storage for a specified time period and with specified permissions. Issuing a SAS that expires after two months provides the required temporary access without granting developers permanent storage-account credentials. Lifecycle policies manage stored data, and storage account keys provide broad access without this time-bound delegation.

finalExplanation: A shared access signature (SAS) delegates restricted access to Azure Storage for a specified time period and with specified permissions. Issuing a SAS that expires after two months provides the required temporary access without granting developers permanent storage-account credentials. Lifecycle policies manage stored data, and storage account keys provide broad access without this time-bound delegation.

You are troubleshooting an application running on an Azure Kubernetes cluster named cluster1. The cluster uses Azure Monitor for containers to monitor it.  
  
The application has sticky sessions enabled on the ingress controller. Some customers have reported many application errors during the past 24 hours.  
  
You need to identify the virtual machines (VMs) where the errors occur. How should you complete the Azure Monitor query?
definition.explanation:
`ago(1d)` creates the required 24-hour time boundary. `distinct ContainerID` returns the container IDs from Cluster1, and `where ContainerID in (ContainerIDs)` restricts container log records to those containers. Standard-error (`stderr`) log records are then counted with `summarize count() by Computer`, which groups the errors by the VM/host computer.

You are developing a solution that will use a multi-partition Azure Cosmos DB database. You plan to use the latest Azure Cosmos DB SDK for development.  
  
The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Send insert and update operations to an Azure Blob storage account.  
- Process changes from all partitions immediately.  
- Allow change processing to be parallelized.  
  
You need to process the Azure Cosmos DB operations.  
  
What are two possible ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create an Azure App Service API and implement the change feed estimator of the SDK. Scale the API by using multiple Azure App Service instances.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a background job in an Azure Kubernetes Service and implement the change feed feature of the SDK.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Azure Function to use a trigger for Azure Cosmos DB. Configure the trigger to connect to the container.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an Azure Function that uses a FeedIterator object that processes the change feed by using the pull model on the container. Use a FeedRange object to parallelize the processing of the change feed across multiple functions.

definition.explanation:
The Azure Cosmos DB trigger for Azure Functions uses the change feed processor internally, detects inserts and updates in the monitored container, and automatically parallelizes processing across container partitions. The change feed pull model can also process changes in parallel by obtaining FeedRange values and using a FeedIterator for each range across multiple function instances; the function code can write each processed change to Azure Blob Storage. The change feed estimator reports outstanding work but does not consume or process the change feed.

**Learn more:** [Read the Azure Cosmos DB change feed](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/read-change-feed) · [Serverless event-based architectures with Azure Cosmos DB and Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/nosql/change-feed-functions)

finalExplanation: The Azure Cosmos DB trigger for Azure Functions uses the change feed processor internally, detects inserts and updates in the monitored container, and automatically parallelizes processing across container partitions. The change feed pull model can also process changes in parallel by obtaining FeedRange values and using a FeedIterator for each range across multiple function instances; the function code can write each processed change to Azure Blob Storage. The change feed estimator reports outstanding work but does not consume or process the change feed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a single Azure AD Service Principal with permission to access Key Vault and use a client secret from within the App Services to access Key Vault.

You have an Azure Service Bus namespace that contains a partitioned queue named `queue1`.  
  
You plan to send a high volume of messages through `queue1` during the next few weeks. Message order will be random. You must minimize the chance that transient failures in individual partitions interrupt message transmission.  
  
You need to use the optimal partition-key configuration for the messages.  
  
Which configuration should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the partition key of messages to the message ID value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable sessions. Set the partition key of messages to the session ID value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable sessions. Ensure that the partition key is different from the session ID value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leave the partition key value as null.

definition.explanation:
Leaving the partition key unset lets Azure Service Bus distribute messages among partitions and retry another partition when the initially selected partition is temporarily unavailable. A set partition key, including a session ID, pins messages to one partition and can cause errors if that partition is unavailable. Sessions are unnecessary because ordered delivery is not required.

**Learn more:** [Partitioned queues and topics - Azure Service Bus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-partitioning)

finalExplanation: Leaving the partition key unset lets Azure Service Bus distribute messages among partitions and retry another partition when the initially selected partition is temporarily unavailable. A set partition key, including a session ID, pins messages to one partition and can cause errors if that partition is unavailable. Sessions are unnecessary because ordered delivery is not required.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing a hospital solution to support these use cases:  
  
- Retrieve the latest patient-status details, even if multiple users in different locations updated the patient record.  
- Retrieve patient health-monitoring data that is the current version or the prior version.  
- After a patient is discharged and all charges are assessed, ensure the patient billing record contains the final charges.  
  
You provision a Cosmos DB NoSQL database and configure the database account’s default consistency level as Strong. You set Indexing Mode to Consistent.  
  
You need to minimize latency and effects on solution availability. Override the default consistency level at the query level to meet the required consistency guarantees for the scenarios.  
  
Which consistency levels should you implement? Each consistency level may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

slots.label: Return the most recent patient status.
Return health monitoring data that is no less than one version behind.
After patient is discharged and all charges are assessed, retrieve the correct billing data with the final charges.

definition.explanation:
Strong consistency returns the most recent committed item version, which is required for the latest patient status and final billing charges. Bounded Staleness sets a maximum lag in item versions; a one-version bound satisfies the health-monitoring requirement. Consistent Prefix and Eventual do not provide the required freshness guarantee.

**Learn more:** [Consistency levels in Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/consistency-levels)

finalExplanation: Strong consistency returns the most recent committed item version, which is required for the latest patient status and final billing charges. Bounded Staleness sets a maximum lag in item versions; a one-version bound satisfies the health-monitoring requirement. Consistent Prefix and Eventual do not provide the required freshness guarantee.

You are building an e-commerce solution that uses a microservice architecture.  
  
You need to design a communication backplane to exchange transactional messages among the different parts of the solution. Messages must be delivered in first-in-first-out (FIFO) order.

definition.explanation:
Azure Service Bus is designed for reliable enterprise and transactional messaging between services. Its message sessions provide guaranteed FIFO processing for related message sequences, making it suitable for an ordered microservice communication backplane.

**Learn more:** [Azure Service Bus message sessions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/message-sessions) · [Compare Azure Storage queues and Service Bus queues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-azure-and-service-bus-queues-compared-contrasted)

finalExplanation: Azure Service Bus is designed for reliable enterprise and transactional messaging between services. Its message sessions provide guaranteed FIFO processing for related message sequences, making it suitable for an ordered microservice communication backplane.

You develop an app that enables users to upload photos and videos to Azure storage. The app uses a Storage REST API call to upload media to a blob storage account named Account1. You have blob storage containers named Container1 and Container2.  
  
Video uploads happen on an irregular basis.  
  
You need to copy particular blobs from Container1 to Container2 whenever a new video is uploaded.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Copy blobs to Container2 by using the Put Blob operation of the Blob Service REST API

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an Event Grid topic that uses the Start-AzureStorageBlobCopy cmdlet

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use AzCopy with the Snapshot switch to copy blobs to Container2

choices.label: D
choices.text: Download the blob to a virtual machine and then upload the blob to Container2

definition.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage emits the `Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated` Event Grid event when a blob is created or replaced through Blob REST APIs. An Event Grid-triggered handler can initiate a server-side blob copy for the qualifying uploaded video, so copying occurs in response to each irregular upload without polling or transferring the blob through a virtual machine.

**Learn more:** [Azure Blob Storage as an Event Grid source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/event-schema-blob-storage) · [Copy Blob (REST API)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/copy-blob)

finalExplanation: Azure Blob Storage emits the `Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated` Event Grid event when a blob is created or replaced through Blob REST APIs. An Event Grid-triggered handler can initiate a server-side blob copy for the qualifying uploaded video, so copying occurs in response to each irregular upload without polling or transferring the blob through a virtual machine.

You must securely expose the APIs through Azure API Management and meet these requirements:  
  
- Only authenticated and authorized clients can access the APIs.  
- Implement control over the number of API calls to prevent abuse and ensure fair use.  
- Perform data transformation and validation for incoming requests and outgoing responses without changing the back-end services.  
- Collect insights into API usage patterns, performance metrics, and anomaly detection.  
  
You need to implement the APIs.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use basic authentication over HTTPS.Apply IP filtering policies.Perform transformation logic in the client application.Enable Azure diagnostics logs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use OAuth 2.0 for authentication and authorization.Apply rate limit policies.Use inbound and outbound policies for transformation.Enable Azure Monitor for detailed analytics.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Require clients to present client certificates.Use response caching policies.Implement request and response transformation in back-end services.Analyze logs with Log Analytics.

choices.label: D

You are developing an application that uses Azure Blob Storage.  
  
The application must read transaction logs for every change made to blobs and blob metadata in the storage account for auditing. The changes must be ordered as they occurred, contain only create, update, delete, and copy operations, and be retained for compliance.  
  
You need to process the transaction logs asynchronously.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Process all Azure Blob storage events by using Azure Event Grid with a subscriber Azure Function app.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable the change feed on the storage account and process all changes for available events.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Process all Azure Storage Analytics logs for successful blob events.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the Azure Monitor HTTP Data Collector API and scan the request body for successful blob events.

definition.explanation:
Azure Blob Storage change feed provides durable, immutable, read-only transaction logs for changes to blobs and blob metadata. Applications can consume the feed asynchronously, either incrementally or in batches, and retention can be configured to meet compliance requirements. The feed captures available blob change events, allowing consumers to filter to the required operation types.

**Learn more:** [Change feed in Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-change-feed) · [Process change feed in Azure Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-blob-change-feed-how-to)

finalExplanation: Azure Blob Storage change feed provides durable, immutable, read-only transaction logs for changes to blobs and blob metadata. Applications can consume the feed asynchronously, either incrementally or in batches, and retention can be configured to meet compliance requirements. The feed captures available blob change events, allowing consumers to filter to the required operation types.

Which event filter should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An advanced filter using a Boolean condition that evaluates multiple data fields, including a season field within the event data

choices.label: B
choices.text: A prefix filter on the event type field that matches the current season's name

choices.label: C

definition.explanation:

definition.template:
az provider register -n Microsoft.KeyVault
resourcegroup=myResourceGroup
az group create --name $resourcegroup --location westus
keyvault_name=myvault$RANDOM

az {{cmd1}} create \
--name $keyvault_name \
--resource-group $resourcegroup \
--location eastus \
--enabled-for-disk-encryption True

az {{cmd2}} create \
--vault-name $keyvault_name \
--name Name1 \
--protection software

az {{cmd3}} create \
--resource-group $resourcegroup \
--name Name2 \
--image Canonical:UbuntuServer:16.04-LTS:latest \
--admin-username azureuser \
--generate-ssh-keys \
--data-disk-sizes-gb 5

--name Name2 \
--disk-encryption-keyvault $keyvault_name \
--key-encryption-key Name1 \
--volume-type {{volume}}

`az keyvault create` creates the Key Vault, and `az keyvault key create` creates a software-protected key in it. `az vm create` provisions the VM. Azure Disk Encryption is enabled with `az vm encryption enable`; `--volume-type all` encrypts both the operating-system and data disks.

definition.stemRaw:
You develop an image-upload service exposed through Azure API Management. Images are analyzed after upload for automatic tagging.  
  
Images over 500 KB are handled by a separate, lower-cost backend. The lower service tier is indicated by an `x-large-request` header. Images exceeding 500 KB must never be processed by backends intended for smaller images and must always be charged the lower price.  
  
Implement API Management policies to ensure images are processed correctly. Complete the inbound policy by selecting the appropriate options.
definition.template:
<inbound>
    <base/>
    <set-variable name="imageSize" value="@(context.Request.Headers["Content-Length"][0])"/>
    <choose>
        <when condition="@(int.Parse(context.Variables.GetValueOrDefault<string>("imageSize"))<512000)">
            <set-header name="x-large-request" exists-action="{{exists_action}}">
                <value>true</value>
            </set-header>
        </when>
        <otherwise>
            <{{policy}} {{backend_attribute}}="{{large-image-host}}"/>
        </otherwise>
    </choose>
</inbound>
definition.explanation:

You are developing a Cosmos DB solution that will be deployed across multiple Azure regions.  
  
Your solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Read operations must never receive write operations out of order.

definition.explanation:

**Learn more:** [Consistency level choices - Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/consistency-levels)

finalExplanation: Consistent prefix consistency ensures reads return a prefix of the committed write sequence, so writes are never observed out of order. It uses single-replica reads, which provides higher read concurrency than consistency levels that require quorum reads, such as bounded staleness.

Add an action that reads IoT temperature data from the Service Bus queue.
Add a condition that compares the temperature against the upper and lower thresholds.
Add an action that sends an email to specified personnel if the temperature is outside of those thresholds.

items: Add a logic app trigger that fires when one or more messages arrive in the queue.
Add a Recurrence trigger that schedules the app to run every 15 minutes.
Add an action that sends an email to specified personnel if the temperature is outside of those thresholds.

Add a logic app action that fires when one or more messages arrive in the queue.
Add a condition that compares the temperature against the upper and lower thresholds.

A Service Bus message-arrival trigger starts the Logic App as soon as messages are available. The workflow then reads the temperature data, evaluates whether it is outside the upper or lower threshold, and sends an email only when that condition is met. A recurrence trigger would not provide immediate alerting, and a Logic App action cannot initiate a workflow run.

You are developing a web application with the Azure SDK. The application accesses data in a zone-redundant BlockBlobStorage storage account.

definition.explanation:

Supplying that saved value in an If-Match header makes the update conditional on the blob still having that same ETag; otherwise Blob Storage returns HTTP 412, requiring the application to reread the latest data before updating.

<policies>

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing a REST web service that customers access through an Azure API Management instance.  
  
The service does not handle conflicts correctly: rather than returning HTTP status code 409, it returns status code 500, and the status-message body contains only the word `conflict`.  
  
You need to ensure that conflicts return the correct response. Complete the policy. Each code segment may be used once, more than once, or not at all.
definition.template:
<{{section_open}}>
  <base />
  <choose>
    <when condition = " @{{response_context}}.Response.StatusCode == 500
                    && {{error_context}}.LastError.Message.Contains "
                              " conflict = " )) " >
      <return-response>
        <{{status_policy}} >
      </return-response>
    </when>
    <otherwise />
  </choose>
</{{section_close}}>
definition.explanation:
The `on-error` section handles policy-processing errors and exposes error details through `context.LastError`. The condition detects the erroneous 500 response and the conflict message. `return-response` stops pipeline processing, and its `set-status` child sets the returned HTTP code to the required 409 conflict response.

**Learn more:** [Error handling in Azure API Management policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-error-handling-policies) · [Azure API Management policy reference – set-status](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/set-status-policy)

finalExplanation: The `on-error` section handles policy-processing errors and exposes error details through `context.LastError`. The condition detects the erroneous 500 response and the conflict message. `return-response` stops pipeline processing, and its `set-status` child sets the returned HTTP code to the required 409 conflict response.

Its scale-out limit is higher than Premium for this scenario. Dedicated hosting does not dynamically scale from events.

definition.stemRaw:
You are building a serverless Java application in Azure and create a new Azure Key Vault for secrets used by a new Azure Functions application.  
  
The application must meet these requirements:  
  
- Reference Azure Key Vault without changing the Java code.  
- Dynamically add or remove Azure Functions host instances according to incoming application events.  
- Keep instances perpetually warm to prevent cold starts.  
- Connect to a VNet.  
- Remove Azure Key Vault authentication when the Azure Function application is deleted.  
  
You need to give the Azure Functions application access to Azure Key Vault.  
  
Which three actions should you take, in order?

slots.answer: Create the Azure Functions app with a Premium plan type.
Create a system-assigned managed identity for the application.
Create an access policy in Azure Key Vault for the application identity.

items: Create a user-assigned managed identity for the application.
Create the Azure Functions app with a Premium plan type.
Create an access policy in Azure Key Vault for the application identity.
Create an SSL certification in Azure Key Vault for the application identity.
Create the Azure Functions app with an App Service plan type.
Create the Azure Functions app with a Consumption plan type.
Create a system-assigned managed identity for the application.
definition.explanation:
Azure Functions Premium provides event-driven scaling, always-ready instances to avoid cold starts, and VNet integration. A system-assigned managed identity shares the function app lifecycle and is deleted with the app. A Key Vault access policy grants that identity access without embedded credentials or Java code changes.

**Learn more:** [Deploy an Azure Function Premium plan with VNet integration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/samples/azure/azure-quickstart-templates/function-premium-vnet-integration/) · [Managed identities for Azure resources](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview)

finalExplanation: Azure Functions Premium provides event-driven scaling, always-ready instances to avoid cold starts, and VNet integration. A system-assigned managed identity shares the function app lifecycle and is deleted with the app. A Key Vault access policy grants that identity access without embedded credentials or Java code changes.

definition.stemRaw:
You develop solutions for Azure.  
  
A .NET application must receive a message whenever an Azure virtual machine completes data processing. Messages must **NOT** persist after the receiving application processes them.  
  
You need to implement the .NET object that receives the messages.  
  
Which object should you use?
definition.explanation:
Azure Service Bus queues support point-to-point delivery to a single consumer. A QueueClient can receive messages using ReceiveAndDelete mode, which treats messages as settled when they are delivered and removes them from the queue, so they do not remain after processing.

You plan to implement an Azure Functions app.  
  
The app must:  
  
- Be triggered by a message placed in an Azure Storage queue.  
- Use the queue name configured by an app setting named `input_queue`.  
- Create an Azure Blob Storage blob whose name matches the message content.  
  
Identify how to reference the queue and blob names in the `function.json` file.
definition.explanation:
Azure Functions resolves an application-setting reference enclosed in percent signs, so `%input_queue%` supplies the queue name. For an Azure Queue trigger, the `{queueTrigger}` binding expression represents the message body; using it in the blob binding path makes the blob name equal to the message content.

**Learn more:** [Azure Functions binding expressions and patterns](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-bindings-expressions-patterns)

For an Azure Queue trigger, the `{queueTrigger}` binding expression represents the message body; using it in the blob binding path makes the blob name equal to the message content.

The microservices must be deployed in the same virtual network and write logs to the same Log Analytics workspace.  
  
You need to deploy the microservices.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

definition.stemRaw:
A company backs up all manufacturing data to Azure Blob Storage. Administrators move blobs from hot storage to the archive tier every month.  
  
You must automatically move blobs to the Archive tier after they have not been modified for 180 days. The path for every item that is not archived must be put in an existing queue. The operation must run automatically once each month. The value of `TierAgeInDays` is set to `-180`.  
  
How should you configure the Logic App? Each trigger or action block can be used once, more than once, or not at all.

slots.answer: Put a message on a queue

items: When there are messages in a queue
Put a message on a queue
definition.explanation:
The operation must run automatically once a month, so the trigger is Recurrence. A Condition then evaluates whether each blob has not been modified for 180 days (using the TierAgeInDays value of -180 against the last-modified date). If the condition is true, the blob meets the archival threshold and the Tier blob action moves it to the Archive tier; if it is false, the item is not archived, so its path is written to the existing queue with Put a message on a queue. List blobs 2 continues enumerating the remaining blobs. The queue receives only the paths of items that were not archived, matching the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Archive a blob](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/archive-blob) · [Access tiers for blob data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/access-tiers-overview)

finalExplanation: The operation must run automatically once a month, so the trigger is Recurrence. A Condition then evaluates whether each blob has not been modified for 180 days (using the TierAgeInDays value of -180 against the last-modified date). If the condition is true, the blob meets the archival threshold and the Tier blob action moves it to the Archive tier; if it is false, the item is not archived, so its path is written to the existing queue with Put a message on a queue. List blobs 2 continues enumerating the remaining blobs. The queue receives only the paths of items that were not archived, matching the requirement.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing an application that enforces a set of governance policies for internal and external services, as well as for applications.  
  
You develop a stateful ASP.NET Core 2.1 web application named PolicyApp and deploy it to an Azure App Service Web App. PolicyApp responds to events from Azure Event Grid and performs policy actions based on those events.  
  
You have the following requirements:  
  
- Authentication events must be used to monitor users as they sign in and sign out.  
- PolicyApp must process all authentication events.  
- Sign-outs must be processed as quickly as possible.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a new Azure Event Grid subscription for all authentication events. Use the subscription to process sign-out events.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a separate Azure Event Grid handler for sign-in and sign-out events.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create separate Azure Event Grid topics and subscriptions for sign-in and sign-out events.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a subject prefix to sign-out events. Create an Azure Event Grid subscription. Configure the subscription to use the subjectBeginsWith filter.

definition.explanation:
Azure Event Grid event subscriptions support subject-prefix filtering through `subjectBeginsWith`, which delivers only events whose subject matches the configured prefix. Giving sign-out events a distinct subject prefix and subscribing with that filter isolates them for direct, prompt processing while other authentication-event processing remains available to PolicyApp.

**Learn more:** [How to filter events for Azure Event Grid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/how-to-filter-events)

finalExplanation: Azure Event Grid event subscriptions support subject-prefix filtering through `subjectBeginsWith`, which delivers only events whose subject matches the configured prefix. Giving sign-out events a distinct subject prefix and subscribing with that filter isolates them for direct, prompt processing while other authentication-event processing remains available to PolicyApp.

You are building a hazard-notification system with one signaling server that causes audio and visual alarms to start and stop.  
  
You use Azure Service Bus to publish alarms. Each alarm controller uses Azure Service Bus to receive alarm signals within a transaction. Alarm events must be logged for auditing. Each transaction record must contain information about the type of alarm that was activated.  
  
You need to implement a reply-trail auditing solution.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assign the value of the hazard message SessionID property to the ReplyToSessionId property.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assign the value of the hazard message MessageId property to the DevileryCount property.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Assign the value of the hazard message SessionID property to the SequenceNumber property.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assign the value of the hazard message MessageId property to the CorrelationId property.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Assign the value of the hazard message SequenceNumber property to the DeliveryCount property.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Assign the value of the hazard message MessageId property to the SequenceNumber property.

definition.explanation:
Azure Service Bus reply routing can use `ReplyToSessionId` to specify the session identifier for replies. A reply is correlated to its triggering message by setting the reply message's `CorrelationId` to the handled message's `MessageId`. This preserves the audit trail between the originating hazard signal and each controller response.

**Learn more:** [Azure Service Bus messages, payloads, and serialization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messages-payloads)

finalExplanation: Azure Service Bus reply routing can use `ReplyToSessionId` to specify the session identifier for replies. A reply is correlated to its triggering message by setting the reply message's `CorrelationId` to the handled message's `MessageId`. This preserves the audit trail between the originating hazard signal and each controller response.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing a solution using the Azure Event Hubs SDK. You create a standard Azure Event Hub with 16 partitions and implement eight event processor clients.  
  
You must dynamically balance the load when an event processor client fails. When one fails, another event processor must continue processing from the exact point where the failure occurred. All events must be aggregated and uploaded to an Azure Blob storage account.  
  
You need to implement event-processing recovery for the solution.  
  
Which SDK features should you use?

blanks.label: Ensure that event process clients mark the position within an event sequence.
Mark the event processor client position within a partition event sequence.

definition.explanation:
An offset is the position (a client-side cursor) of an event within a partition's event sequence, so it fills blank1, which asks for the mechanism that identifies the position within an event sequence. Checkpointing is defined by Microsoft as the process by which readers mark or commit their position within a partition event sequence, which matches blank2 almost verbatim and is what lets a surviving event processor resume from the exact point where the failed one stopped. The two dropdowns require different answers: the offset is the position value, while the checkpoint is the durable commit of that offset to storage that enables recovery and load rebalancing, so answering Checkpoint for both is incorrect.

**Learn more:** [Event Hubs features and terminology](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/event-hubs-features) · [Balance partition load across multiple instances](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-hubs/event-processor-balance-partition-load)

finalExplanation: An offset is the position (a client-side cursor) of an event within a partition's event sequence, so it fills blank1, which asks for the mechanism that identifies the position within an event sequence. Checkpointing is defined by Microsoft as the process by which readers mark or commit their position within a partition event sequence, which matches blank2 almost verbatim and is what lets a surviving event processor resume from the exact point where the failed one stopped. The two dropdowns require different answers: the offset is the position value, while the checkpoint is the durable commit of that offset to storage that enables recovery and load rebalancing, so answering Checkpoint for both is incorrect.

You are developing several microservices for deployment to a new Azure Kubernetes Service cluster. The microservices manage data stored in Azure Cosmos DB and Azure Blob storage. The data is protected by using customer-managed keys stored in Azure Key Vault.  
  
You must automate rotation for all Azure Key Vault keys while also allowing manual key rotation. Keys must be rotated every three months. Notifications for expiring keys must be sent before the keys expire.  
  
You need to configure key rotation and enable key-expiry notifications.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create and configure a new Azure Event Grid instance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create and assign an Azure Key Vault access policy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create and configure a key rotation policy during key creation.

definition.explanation:
An Azure Key Vault key rotation policy can schedule automatic generation of new key versions at a defined interval and still permits on-demand rotation. Its notification action triggers Azure Event Grid key-near-expiry events before expiration; configuring Event Grid enables those events to be routed to a notification handler.

**Learn more:** [Configure cryptographic key auto-rotation in Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/keys/how-to-configure-key-rotation) · [Azure Key Vault as Event Grid source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/event-grid/event-schema-key-vault)

finalExplanation: An Azure Key Vault key rotation policy can schedule automatic generation of new key versions at a defined interval and still permits on-demand rotation. Its notification action triggers Azure Event Grid key-near-expiry events before expiration; configuring Event Grid enables those events to be routed to a notification handler.

definition.stemRaw:
You developed a Web App for your company that provides services and must run across multiple regions.  
  
You need notification whenever the Web App consumes more than 85 percent of the available CPU cores during a five-minute period, while minimizing costs.  
  
Which command should you use?
definition.template:
az monitor metrics alert create -n myAlert -g myResourceGroup
--scopes targetResourceID --condition "{{condition}} > 85"
{{window_option}} 5m
definition.explanation:
Metric alert conditions use an aggregation and metric name, so `avg Percentage CPU > 85` evaluates average CPU percentage. `--window-size 5m` configures the five-minute aggregation window. `--evaluation-frequency` is only the cadence at which the rule is evaluated.

**Learn more:** [az monitor metrics alert create](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/monitor/metrics/alert?view=azure-cli-latest#az-monitor-metrics-alert-create) · [Supported metrics for Microsoft.Web/sites](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-web-sites-metrics)

finalExplanation: Metric alert conditions use an aggregation and metric name, so `avg Percentage CPU > 85` evaluates average CPU percentage. `--window-size 5m` configures the five-minute aggregation window. `--evaluation-frequency` is only the cadence at which the rule is evaluated.
